S48.01.needs: a signed-in account with voice access; a microphone; a cloud model selected
S48.01.note: The button shows only when the message box is empty, voice access is granted and the model is a managed cloud model (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx, voiceManaged).
steps: Sign in and open an existing chat that already has messages.
Leave the message box empty and make sure the selected model is a cloud model.
Click the round waveform button named 'Start voice mode' at the right end of the message box.
Look: the message box is replaced by the voice bar, and the chat you opened is still on screen. Compare with Expected: voice starts bound to that chat.
S48.01.where: Open an existing chat from the sidebar > empty message box > round button 'Start voice mode' (waveform icon, right end of the box)

S48.02.needs: a signed-in account with voice access; a microphone; a cloud model selected
S48.02.note: No separate control for a new voice chat was found; it uses the same button as S48.01. Whether the new chat is created at call start was not traced in the UI.
steps: Click 'New chat' in the sidebar.
Leave the message box empty.
Click 'Start voice mode'.
Look: a voice call starts on the new chat. Compare with Expected: a brand-new chat is created for the call.
S48.02.where: Sidebar > 'New chat' > empty message box > round button 'Start voice mode' (right end of the box)

S48.03.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
steps: Open a chat with several earlier messages.
Click 'Start voice mode'.
Look at the header: the word 'Voice' appears next to the logo.
Speak one sentence and wait for the reply.
Look: your words and the reply appear in the same list as the typed messages, above the voice bar. Compare with Expected.
S48.03.where: Open a chat that already has messages > round button 'Start voice mode' (right end of the message box)

labels.text: Hide the transcript and focus the orb

S48.04.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.04.note: No separate full-screen page was found. The closest is this focus mode, which fades the transcript inside the same voice view.
steps: Start a voice call (see S48.01).
Click the orb in the middle of the screen.
Look: the transcript fades and the orb is the focus of the view.
Click the orb again and look for the name 'Show the transcript again' on it.
Compare with Expected: a separate full-screen voice layout.
S48.04.where: Voice view > round orb in the middle of the screen (its name is 'Hide the transcript and focus the orb')

S48.05.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.05.note: The word 'Listening' is not drawn on screen (the orb label is hidden in the voice view). The visible cue is the orb; the word is only in the screen-reader announcement.
steps: Start a voice call (see S48.01) and wait until the call is idle and waiting for you.
Look at the orb: it shows its listening state.
Optional: with VoiceOver on, listen for the announcement 'Listening'.
Compare with Expected: a visible and announced listening state.
S48.05.where: Voice view > round orb in the middle of the screen

S48.06.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.06.note: The word 'Speaking' is not drawn on screen; the visible cue is the orb.
steps: Start a voice call and ask a short question.
Wait for the assistant's reply to start playing.
Look at the orb: it changes while the reply plays.
Optional: with VoiceOver on, listen for 'Assistant is speaking'.
Compare with Expected: a visible speaking state.
S48.06.where: Voice view > round orb in the middle of the screen

S48.07.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.07.note: The line shows when a tool runs or the backend is busy. Which requests trigger it depends on the model and the task.
steps: Start a voice call.
Ask for something that needs a tool or a lookup.
Look under the orb for a spinner and the text 'Working on your request', with a 'Stop the task' button beside it.
Compare with Expected: a visible thinking or working state while the assistant works.
S48.07.where: Voice view > line with a spinner under the orb reading 'Working on your request' (with a 'Stop the task' button)

S48.08.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.08.note: No separate waveform bar was found; the orb itself follows the audio level (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/VoiceOrb.tsx).
steps: Start a voice call.
Speak a long sentence at normal volume.
Look at the orb: it grows and shrinks with your voice.
Wait for a reply and look at the orb again.
Compare with Expected: a visual follows the live audio level.
S48.08.where: Voice view > round orb in the middle of the screen

S48.09.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.09.note: Pressing Space while the voice bar's text field is empty also toggles mute (VoiceComposer.tsx).
steps: Start a voice call.
Click the round microphone button in the bottom bar.
Look: the icon changes to a crossed-out microphone, the button turns red, and its name becomes 'Turn on microphone'.
Look at the call timer: it keeps running.
Click the button again and check the microphone is back on. Compare with Expected: mute without ending the call.
S48.09.where: Voice view > bottom voice bar > round microphone button (named 'Turn off microphone')

S48.10.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.10.note: Escape also ends the call. Settling of usage is not visible on screen.
steps: Start a voice call and talk for a moment.
Click the X button 'End voice session'.
Look: the voice bar closes, the normal message box comes back, and the call timer stops.
Compare with Expected: the call is closed.
S48.10.where: Voice view > bottom voice bar > round X button named 'End voice session' (right end)

S48.11.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.11.note: The paused notice says the call is closed while paused, so check whether resume keeps the same conversation against Expected.
steps: Start a voice call.
Click the round '+' button at the left of the bottom bar.
Click 'Pause call' under the menu heading 'In this chat'. Hmm: the item sits under the heading 'This call'.
Look: a notice says the call is paused and a 'Resume' button appears.
Click 'Resume' and check the call comes back without starting over. Compare with Expected.
S48.11.where: Voice view > round '+' button at the left of the bottom bar > menu 'In this chat' > 'Pause call'

S48.13.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.13.note: No hands-free switch was found in the code. The check is only whether a second turn needs no tap.
steps: Start a voice call.
Say one thing and wait for the reply to finish.
Say a second thing without touching any button.
Look: the orb returns to listening and takes the second turn without a tap.
S48.13.where: No on or off switch found; the effect shows across turns in the voice view

S48.14.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access; a live voice service
S48.14.note: Unverified in the code. It depends on the external voice service, so the result may vary by session.
steps: Start a voice call and ask for a long answer.
While the orb shows the speaking state and the reply is playing, start talking over it.
Look: the spoken reply stops and the orb moves to listening. Compare with Expected.
S48.14.where: Seen in the voice view while the orb shows the speaking state

S48.15.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.15.note: The dots appear only when there are 2 to 16 voices.
steps: Start a voice call.
Click the gear button 'Voice settings'.
Click 'Next voice' and look at the name in the middle change.
Click the voice name dots below, if shown, to pick another voice.
Close the dialog, let the assistant speak, and check the voice matches the name you chose. Compare with Expected.
S48.15.where: Voice view > gear button 'Voice settings' (next to 'Voice' in the header) > voice name between the arrows 'Previous voice' and 'Next voice'

S48.16.needs: a signed-in account with voice access; a speaker or headphones
S48.16.note: Unfinished. apps/web/public/voice-samples/manifest.json is empty, so 'Play sample' does not appear until the sample files are generated (plan owner step: OPENAI_API_KEY=<server key> node scripts/generate-voice-samples.mjs, then commit apps/web/public/voice-samples).
steps: Start a voice call and open 'Voice settings'.
Look under the voice name and arrows for the button 'Play sample'.
Click 'Play sample' and listen.
Compare with Expected: a sample of the voice plays before you choose it.
S48.16.where: Voice view > gear button 'Voice settings' > under the voice name, button 'Play sample'

S48.17.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.17.note: Whether recognition follows the choice is confirmed only by a live call.
steps: Start a voice call and open 'Voice settings'.
Click the 'Language' picker and choose a language other than 'Auto-detect'.
Close the dialog and speak in that language.
Compare with Expected: the spoken language is used for recognition. Check the transcript and reply.
S48.17.where: Voice view > gear button 'Voice settings' > 'Language' picker (first option 'Auto-detect')

S48.19.needs: a browser that can switch speaker output (the code checks for this); a second audio output device
S48.19.note: The picker checks browser support before switching output. What it shows in an unsupported browser was not traced.
steps: Start a voice call and open 'Voice settings'.
Click the 'Audio output' button and open its list.
Choose a different speaker from the list.
Let the assistant speak and check the sound comes from the chosen speaker. Compare with Expected.
S48.19.where: Voice view > gear button 'Voice settings' > 'Audio output' button (shows 'System default' or a device name)

S48.21.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
steps: Start a voice call.
Click the round '+' button at the left of the bottom bar.
Click 'Captions' under the heading 'This call'.
Speak, and let the assistant reply.
Look for lines labelled 'You' and 'Assistant' appearing as text. Compare with Expected: captions of both speakers.
S48.21.where: Voice view > round '+' button at the left of the bottom bar > 'This call' > 'Captions'

S48.22.needs: a microphone; a speaker or headphones; a signed-in account with voice access
S48.22.note: If a voice turn cannot be saved, a warning toast appears (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx).
steps: Make a short voice call with two spoken turns.
Click the X button 'End voice session' to finish the call.
Look at the chat: your spoken turns and the replies appear as messages in order.
Reload the page and check the same messages are still there. Compare with Expected.
S48.22.where: Open the chat after the voice call (the voice turns are saved as messages in that chat)

S48.26.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access; a task that uses a tool
S48.26.note: The link under the reply shows only while voice mode is on (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx). The text 'Thought for' is built from a number in VoiceActivityAffordance.tsx.
steps: Start a voice call and ask for a task that uses a tool.
Look above the orb for the tool row with the tool name and result.
Scroll up in the chat while the call stays open and click the link under an assistant reply.
Look: the 'Activity' panel opens and lists the steps. Press Escape to close it. Compare with Expected.
S48.26.where: Voice view > tool row above the orb after a tool runs; then, in the chat above, the 'Stopped thinking' or 'Thought for' link under an assistant reply opens 'Activity'

S48.27.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access; a task that asks for approval
S48.27.note: Which buttons appear depends on the action's scopes (apps/web/features/chat/components/approvals/ToolApprovalCard.tsx).
steps: Start a voice call.
Ask for an action that needs approval, such as one that changes something.
Look for the approval card in the voice view.
Click 'Allow once' or 'Deny'.
Look: the card closes and the call continues without leaving voice. Compare with Expected.
S48.27.where: Voice view > card above the orb for an action that needs approval, with buttons such as 'Allow once', 'Allow for this chat' and 'Deny'

S48.28.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access; a task that creates a file
S48.28.note: Only files with paths under /api/files/ are shown as links (VoiceModeSurface.tsx).
steps: Start a voice call and ask for a task that creates a document.
Look under the tool row for 'Open' with a file name.
Click the link.
Look: the file opens in a new browser tab. Compare with Expected.
S48.28.where: Voice view > under the tool row, a link 'Open' followed by the file name (images show as a picture link)

S48.36.needs: a microphone; a signed-in account with voice access; a way to drop the connection (for example Wi-Fi off)
S48.36.note: There is no button; the state appears only when the connection drops.
steps: Start a voice call.
Turn off Wi-Fi for a few seconds.
Look above the orb for 'Reconnecting, attempt' with a spinner and a count.
Turn Wi-Fi back on and look again: the line goes away and the call continues, or an error with 'Try again' appears. Compare with Expected.
S48.36.where: Voice view > a line 'Reconnecting, attempt N of M' above the orb when the connection drops

S48.37.needs: an account whose voice usage is used up
S48.37.note: The notice text comes from the server error, so its wording is not fixed in the code.
steps: Use voice until the voice allowance is used up.
Look in the voice view for the usage notice with the buttons 'Upgrade' and 'Continue in text'.
Click 'Continue in text' and check you return to the text message box in the same chat. Compare with Expected.
S48.37.where: Voice view > notice with 'Upgrade' and 'Continue in text' when voice usage runs out

S48.38.needs: a signed-in account with voice access; a microphone
S48.38.note: The bottom voice bar also has a text field that sends a normal turn without leaving voice (VoiceComposer.tsx).
steps: In a call on a chat that has messages, click the X button 'End voice session'.
Look: the normal message box returns in the same chat, with the earlier voice turns above it.
Type a message and send it.
Compare with Expected: the send goes into the same unfinished conversation.
S48.38.where: Voice view > X button 'End voice session' at the right end of the bottom bar (or Escape), then the normal message box

S48.39.note: The code starts voice on the open chat's conversation ID and loads earlier context for that conversation; I did not find a sidebar label for the earlier chat, and the needs value of a paid account is a guess.
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has a voice conversation or earlier turns.
Leave the message field empty so the round button on the right shows its voice icon.
Click the button labelled Start voice mode.
Check that the voice view opens for that same chat and that the assistant answers with the earlier turns in mind (ask it what you talked about before).
S48.39.where: Open an earlier chat from the sidebar, then with the message field empty click Start voice mode

S48.40.needs: a computer paired with the Desktop app
S48.40.note: The remote coding page is at the route apps/web/app/code/computer/page.tsx, with a Task box that has a Start voice input button (dictation) and a Send to computer button, but RemoteComputerLink, which should link to it, has no caller in apps or features, so I could not confirm a menu path; the page offers dictated task text, not a voice conversation.

S48.41.note: Stop the task appears only when the agent status is shown and calls cancelBackendWork; I found no separate control that stops only the spoken reply (the only other stop-like labels are Do not send that and Stop sharing your camera), so the spoken-reply half of Expected is not confirmed.
steps: Open a chat, leave the message field empty and click Start voice mode.
Ask for an action that takes a while, such as a web search.
While the status line with a spinner is showing, click Stop the task.
Check that the status line goes away, the call stays open and the voice conversation still works. The task should stop without ending the call.
S48.41.where: Start voice mode, then while a task is running click Stop the task
